1	FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 is the conductor of that electrical branch and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, and a reference below to the electrical branch is a reference to the branch supplied by the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. The description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel connected to the branch conductor 102, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.
4	
5	A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of the connector channels, its measurement of the branch current is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.
6	
7	An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries communications between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, including the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports.
8	
9	FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The isolated local bus 108 couples the edge controller 106 to the contactor 122 and the control-pilot interface 126 of the first connector channel 120. The edge controller 106 is also coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.
10	
11	The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.
12	
13	FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. The edge controller 106 stores, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current requested for the session at that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value is a value stored for the session and used in distributing the remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels.
14	
15	A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the edge controller 106 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 and lead to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104, both of which are shown in FIG. 1, and to the connector current sensor of each connector channel, such as the connector current sensor 124 shown in FIG. 2.
16	
17	FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.
18	
19	At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the spare capacity of the branch.
20	
21	At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained.
22	
23	At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.
24	
25	At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.
26	
27	At the staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the process returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command. The process proceeds to the ordered shedding step 212 if the measured branch current remains above the branch current limit for a verification interval after that reduced pilot command has been sent.
28	
29	At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.
30	
31	The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A measured branch current that remains above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent therefore causes a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212, and no contactor is opened at that step while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
32	
33	At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current value. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.
34	
35	At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Reclosure of the contactor is withheld until the three conditions are satisfied together, and a connector channel whose contactor has been reclosed takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.
36	
37	The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.
38	
39	During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.
40	
41	Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.
42	
43	The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. Responsive to a command received at the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of one commanded connector channel, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected when the association is carried out, rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.
44	
45	The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.
46

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 is the conductor of that electrical branch and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, and a reference below to the electrical branch is a reference to the branch supplied by the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. The description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel connected to the branch conductor 102, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of the connector channels, its measurement of the branch current is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries communications between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, including the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The isolated local bus 108 couples the edge controller 106 to the contactor 122 and the control-pilot interface 126 of the first connector channel 120. The edge controller 106 is also coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. The edge controller 106 stores, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current requested for the session at that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value is a value stored for the session and used in distributing the remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the edge controller 106 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 and lead to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104, both of which are shown in FIG. 1, and to the connector current sensor of each connector channel, such as the connector current sensor 124 shown in FIG. 2.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the spare capacity of the branch.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.

At the staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the process returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command. The process proceeds to the ordered shedding step 212 if the measured branch current remains above the branch current limit for a verification interval after that reduced pilot command has been sent.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A measured branch current that remains above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent therefore causes a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212, and no contactor is opened at that step while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current value. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Reclosure of the contactor is withheld until the three conditions are satisfied together, and a connector channel whose contactor has been reclosed takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. Responsive to a command received at the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of one commanded connector channel, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected when the association is carried out, rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

The FIG. 2 brief was over the 2800 character limit and its closing sentence was cut off mid-word ("semantic identifiers onl"); it is rewritten to a complete, compact brief of 2707 characters that keeps every disclosed body, contact, crossing and occlusion (dashed channel boundary, contactor square on the incoming supply, connector current sensor circle on the run to the vehicle connector, sensing line to the edge controller, control-pilot interface and its line to the vehicle connector, electric vehicle, and the two branches of the isolated local bus) and all seven numerals. The FIG. 4 brief was trimmed to 2630 characters by condensing a shape-spacing sentence, and its leader instruction now targets the broad interior of each shape rather than an exact centre point. No claim, no other specification text and no numeral assignment was touched; the numeral table is unchanged and still matches the text and figure lists.
reasoning: Both reviewer findings were genuine and were fixed exactly as scoped. Numeral 210 appeared nowhere earlier in the description, so 'At the staged reduction step 210' had no antecedent; changing 'the' to 'a' aligns it with steps 202, 204, 206, 208, 212, 214 and 216 and required no technical change, since the content of the step (compare measured branch current with the branch current limit, send a reduced pilot command, proceed to ordered shedding after the verification interval) is unchanged and remains the disclosed behaviour.

The FIG. 1 fix adds a placement constraint, not structure. The description already says the non-charging load 118 is connected to the branch conductor 102 and that the branch current sensor 104 measures the total current carried by that conductor, and the operation subtracts the measured non-charging branch load from the branch current limit. If the renderer tapped the non-charging load upstream of the sensor, the drawing would show a load the sensor does not see, which is the opposite of what the allocation depends on. Constraining all three drops to the right of the sensor is the minimum change that makes the sheet consistent with the text.

The FIG. 2 brief was the only real filing blocker: it exceeded the length gate and, because it had been cut short, ended in a fragment, which is an unfinished marker in a figure file. I rewrote rather than patched, cutting the verbose justification sentences ('the run has no free end and does not travel towards the left edge of the sheet', 'Neither end of this joining line is free', 'This is the only square outline in the drawing area', 'This is the only circle in the drawing area') because those were renderer controls and negative restatements, not invention geometry. content.content:
19:At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the spare capacity of the branch.
21:At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained.
27:At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the process returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command. The process proceeds to the ordered shedding step 212 if the measured branch current remains above the branch current limit for a verification interval after that reduced pilot command has been sent.
29:At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.
31:The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A measured branch current that remains above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent therefore causes a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212, and no contactor is opened at that step while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
33:At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current value. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.
35:At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Reclosure of the contactor is withheld until the three conditions are satisfied together, and a connector channel whose contactor has been reclosed takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.

1	1. An apparatus for controlling charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch current limit that is lower than a sum of current ratings of the vehicle connectors, the apparatus comprising:
2	
3	a plurality of connector channels, each connector channel comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective one of the vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the respective one of the vehicle connectors, and a control-pilot interface, each connector channel being associated with a local connector identifier;
4	
5	a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current in the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector channels; and
6	
7	a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels, to the connector current sensors of the plurality of connector channels, to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels and to the branch current sensor, the controller being configured to:
8	
9	store, for each active connector channel of the plurality of connector channels, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value;
10	
11	at each allocation interval of a succession of allocation intervals, subtract a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assign the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and distribute a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel;
12	
13	send the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, and verify the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel;
14	
15	receive a measured branch current from the branch current sensor;
16	
17	send a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit; and
18	
19	responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, open the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
20	
21	2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to measure the branch current with the branch current sensor after each opening of one of the contactors in the stored shedding order, and to open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
22	
23	3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to withhold reclosure of the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until the connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.
24	
25	4. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a local fault indicator, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate the local fault indicator.
26	
27	5. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels.
28	
29	6. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface, to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during an outage of the network interface, to continue charging sessions that are already authorized subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to opening the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in the stored shedding order responsive to the measured branch current.

I repaired the three failing sheets; the application text needed no change, since the review reported no text or source-fidelity findings.

**FIG. 1** (leader/endpoint failures on 100, 104, 118, 120, 140): the branch current sensor is now an empty rectangle that interrupts the branch conductor line, giving 104 a closed blank interior to land in instead of a small square sitting next to the dashed sensing line the endpoint reviewers kept hitting. The sensing connection now leaves the bottom side of that rectangle. Numeral 100 moved off the dashed boundary line to a point just inside the enclosure in blank space, which is what a dot-terminated leader needs. Every entry is reworded to state where the *leader endpoint* lies, since reviewers read the old "leader ends well inside X" as specifying numeral placement rather than the endpoint.

**FIG. 3** (106 stuck in a rejected coordinate cluster): 106 no longer targets the boundary of the large rectangle. The brief now states that a blank area remains inside the large rectangle, right of the service input and between the network interface and the nonvolatile memory, and 106 targets that area.

**FIG. 4** (semantic review: the second return path was drawn as a loop on the top rectangle): the path is now specified as three named segments with an explicit start (right edge of the bottom rectangle 216), an explicit route outboard of the square terminator, and an explicit finish on the *top* edge of the topmost rectangle 202, so the return no longer competes with the left-hand return for the left edge and cannot be read as a right-edge-to-left-edge loop.

I also corrected two rule compliance points inherited in FIG. 1: placement is now described against the drawing area rather than the sheet edge, and I dropped a blank-band requirement that existed only to make label room.

FIG. 1: the branch current sensor is now an empty rectangle interrupting the branch conductor line so numeral 104 has a closed blank interior to terminate in, the dashed sensing connection leaves the bottom side of that rectangle, and numeral 100 moved off the dashed enclosure boundary to a point just inside the enclosure where a dot terminator can be drawn. Every numeral entry in FIG. 1, FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 now states where the leader endpoint lies, answering the reviewers who read the old phrasing as specifying the numeral position rather than the endpoint. FIG. 3: numeral 106 no longer targets the boundary of the large rectangle; the brief establishes a blank interior area right of the service input and between the network interface and the nonvolatile memory, and 106 targets that area, which also breaks the rejected coordinate cluster. A dashed line leaves the bottom side of the branch current sensor rectangle and runs down and left to the top side of the edge controller block, representing the sensing connection. # FIG. 1

A flat schematic system diagram in plain black line work on white, no shading and no words other than the reference numerals listed below. All line work stays well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins.

A dashed rectangle encloses the whole diagram and represents the charging installation, shown schematically. It is inset well inside the drawing area, its four sides standing clear of the drawing area boundary and of the filing margins.

Inside it, one horizontal solid line runs across the upper part and represents the branch conductor. Its left end stops at the left side of the dashed rectangle, meeting and terminating on that side to indicate the incoming supply; it does not continue past that side, and no line work lies to the left of the dashed rectangle. Its right end stops short of the right side of the dashed rectangle, above the rightmost of the three blocks described below.

An empty rectangle stands on this horizontal line in its left portion and represents the branch current sensor. The horizontal line meets its left side and leaves its right side, so that the rectangle interrupts the line and its interior is blank and closed.

Three empty rectangular blocks of equal size stand in a row across the lower part, plainly spaced apart, each large enough to hold a clear blank interior. The leftmost is a first connector channel, the middle a second connector channel, the rightmost a non-charging load.

A short vertical line drops from the horizontal line to the top edge of each of the three blocks, connecting all three in parallel. All three drops lie to the right of the branch current sensor.

A further empty rectangular block sits below and left of the leftmost block and represents an edge controller.

A solid line leaves the right side of the edge controller block and runs horizontally beneath the row of three blocks as an isolated local bus. One short vertical branch rises from this bus line to the bottom edge of the leftmost block and another to the bottom edge of the middle block. The bus line does not touch the rightmost block.

A dashed line leaves the bottom side of the branch current sensor rectangle and runs down and left to the top side of the edge controller block, representing the sensing connection. It stays left of the three vertical drops, touches none of the three blocks, and crosses neither the horizontal line, any vertical drop, nor the bus line.

Part names below are semantic identifiers only and do not appear as drawing text. Each numeral sits clear of the line work on a short straight leader that crosses no other leader and no line work.

1	FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 is the conductor of that electrical branch and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, and a reference below to the electrical branch is a reference to the branch supplied by the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. The description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel connected to the branch conductor 102, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.
4	
5	A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of the connector channels, its measurement of the branch current is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.
6	
7	An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries communications between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, including the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports.
8	
9	FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The isolated local bus 108 couples the edge controller 106 to the contactor 122 and the control-pilot interface 126 of the first connector channel 120. The edge controller 106 is also coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel by a sensing connection, and reads the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124 over that connection. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.
10	
11	The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.
12	
13	FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. The edge controller 106 stores, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current requested for the session at that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value is a value stored for the session and used in distributing the remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels.
14	
15	A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the edge controller 106 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 and lead to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104, both of which are shown in FIG. 1.
16	
17	FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.
18	
19	At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the spare capacity of the branch.
20	
21	At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained.
22	
23	At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.
24	
25	At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.
26	
27	At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the process returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command. The process proceeds to the ordered shedding step 212 if the measured branch current remains above the branch current limit for a verification interval after that reduced pilot command has been sent.
28	
29	At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.
30	
31	The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A measured branch current that remains above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent therefore causes a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212, and no contactor is opened at that step while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
32	
33	At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current value. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.
34	
35	At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Reclosure of the contactor is withheld until the three conditions are satisfied together, and a connector channel whose contactor has been reclosed takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.
36	
37	The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.
38	
39	During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.
40	
41	Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.
42	
43	The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. Responsive to a command received at the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of one commanded connector channel, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected when the association is carried out, rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.
44	
45	The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.
46

A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the edge controller 106 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 and lead to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104, both of which are shown in FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the spare capacity of the branch.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the process returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command. The process proceeds to the ordered shedding step 212 if the measured branch current remains above the branch current limit for a verification interval after that reduced pilot command has been sent.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A measured branch current that remains above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent therefore causes a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212, and no contactor is opened at that step while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current value. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Reclosure of the contactor is withheld until the three conditions are satisfied together, and a connector channel whose contactor has been reclosed takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. Responsive to a command received at the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of one commanded connector channel, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected when the association is carried out, rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

# FIG. 2

A flat schematic diagram of one connector channel in plain black line work on white, no shading and no words in the drawing area other than the reference numerals listed below. All line work stays well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins.

A dashed rectangle occupies the left and central portion of the drawing area and represents the first connector channel.

A solid vertical line enters from above, crosses the top side of the dashed rectangle in its left portion and continues downward inside it, as the incoming branch supply. A contactor interrupts this line in the upper half of the rectangle, shown schematically as a small empty square outline straddling the line.

Below the contactor the vertical line reaches a corner at about the middle height of the rectangle and turns to the right, running horizontally to the left side of an empty rectangular block that straddles the right side of the dashed rectangle and represents the vehicle connector, shown schematically.

A small empty circle outline straddles this horizontal run about midway between the corner and the vehicle connector block and represents the connector current sensor, shown schematically.

A straight solid vertical line leaves the lower side of that circle and runs downward to below the dashed rectangle, crossing the lower side of the dashed rectangle and ending free a short distance beneath it. This is the sensing connection between the connector current sensor and the edge controller, and it carries no reference numeral of its own.

An empty rectangular block sits in the lower region of the dashed rectangle, to the right of that downward line and to the left of the vehicle connector block, and represents the control-pilot interface. One solid line leaves the right side of that block, runs horizontally to the right, then turns upward and rises to the lower edge of the vehicle connector block.

Right of the dashed rectangle a larger rounded rectangle represents an electric vehicle, shown schematically. A short solid line joins the right side of the vehicle connector block to the left side of the rounded rectangle.

A solid horizontal line enters from the left of the drawing area and crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle in its lower region, as the isolated local bus. Inside the rectangle this bus line continues to the right at that same height, crosses the downward sensing line at a right angle, and meets the left side of the control-pilot interface block. A short vertical branch rises from the bus line, left of the incoming supply line, to the left side of the square outline of the contactor.

The part names listed below are semantic identifiers only and do not appear as drawing text. Each reference numeral sits on a short straight leader clear of the line work and crossing no other leader.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 108 isolated local bus: leader ends on the bus line left of the dashed rectangle.
- 120 first connector channel: leader ends on the dashed rectangle.
- 122 contactor: leader ends on the square outline straddling the vertical line.
- 124 connector current sensor: leader ends on the upper part of the circle outline straddling the horizontal run.
- 126 control-pilot interface: leader ends well inside the lower block within the dashed rectangle.
- 128 vehicle connector: leader ends well inside the block straddling the right side.
- 130 electric vehicle: leader ends well inside the rounded rectangle.
