# FIG. 4

A flat process flow diagram in plain black line work on white, no shading and no words other than the reference numerals listed below. All line work stays well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins.

Eight empty shapes stand in one vertical column down the centre of the drawing area, evenly spaced from top to bottom. In order from the top they are: a rectangle, a rectangle, a rectangle, a rectangle, a diamond, a rectangle, a diamond, a rectangle. Each shape has a clear blank interior.

A vertical solid line with an arrowhead at its lower end joins each shape of the column to the shape immediately below it, the arrowhead touching the upper edge of that lower shape where it is a rectangle and its upper vertex where it is a diamond.

The line running down to the bottom rectangle leaves the lower vertex of the lower diamond, and represents the case where no welded-contactor condition is recorded. A short horizontal line leaves the right vertex of the lower diamond, runs to the right and ends in an arrowhead at a small solid square terminator, representing the case where a welded-contactor condition has been recorded.

Two return paths run outside the column, one on each side; each stays clear of the column and of the other.

The left return path leaves the left vertex of the upper diamond with no arrowhead, runs left, rises alongside the column, then runs rightward at the mid height of the topmost rectangle into one arrowhead that points right and touches the left-hand vertical side of that rectangle.

The right return path starts with no arrowhead at the right-hand vertical side of the bottom rectangle, at the mid height of that rectangle. It runs rightward, then upward farther right than the square terminator and than every shape in the column, clear of the terminator, rising the full height of the column, then turns leftward at the mid height of the topmost rectangle and ends in one arrowhead that points left and touches the right-hand vertical side of that rectangle.

Part names below are semantic identifiers only and do not appear as drawing text. Each numeral sits on a short straight leader clear of the line work, crossing no other leader, and ending well inside the shape named for it.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 202 available current determination step: leader ends well inside the topmost rectangle.
- 204 sustaining and deficit assignment step: leader ends well inside the second shape from the top.
- 206 pilot command step: leader ends well inside the third shape from the top.
- 208 connector verification step: leader ends well inside the fourth shape from the top.
- 210 staged reduction step: leader ends well inside the upper of the two diamonds.
- 212 ordered shedding step: leader ends well inside the rectangle that lies between the two diamonds.
- 214 welded-contactor isolation step: leader ends well inside the lower of the two diamonds.
- 216 conditional reclosure step: leader ends well inside the bottom rectangle.

content.content:
1	Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection.
4	
5	Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization. Connectivity in a below grade parking structure or a remote depot is intermittent. A controller that treats loss of connectivity as a reason to stop charging strands vehicles that were already authorized, while a controller that treats loss of connectivity as permission to charge without restraint abandons the branch limit that the last accepted configuration established, and abandons the accounting record that billing depends on.
6	
7	A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
8	
9	There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.
10

1	1. An apparatus for controlling charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch current limit that is lower than a sum of current ratings of the vehicle connectors, the apparatus comprising:
2	
3	a plurality of connector channels, each connector channel comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective one of the vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the respective one of the vehicle connectors, and a control-pilot interface, each connector channel being associated with a local connector identifier;
4	
5	a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current in the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector channels; and
6	
7	a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels, to the connector current sensors of the plurality of connector channels, to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels and to the branch current sensor, the controller being configured to:
8	
9	store, for each active connector channel of the plurality of connector channels, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value;
10	
11	at each allocation interval of a succession of allocation intervals, subtract a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assign the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and distribute a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel;
12	
13	send the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, and verify the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel;
14	
15	receive a measured branch current from the branch current sensor;
16	
17	send a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit; and
18	
19	responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, open the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
20	
21	2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to measure the branch current with the branch current sensor after each opening of one of the contactors in the stored shedding order, and to open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
22	
23	3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to withhold reclosure of the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until the connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.
24	
25	4. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a local fault indicator, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate the local fault indicator.
26	
27	5. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels.
28	
29	6. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface, to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during an outage of the network interface, to continue charging sessions that are already authorized subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to opening the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in the stored shedding order responsive to the measured branch current.

I fixed the four drawing briefs; no application text needed changing.

**FIG. 1** - the bus line now terminates beneath the middle block, well left of the non-charging load, and the brief states positively that the only line work meeting the rightmost block is the vertical drop to its top edge.

**FIG. 2** - re-laid out to remove the ambiguous routing that produced T-junctions. The sensing line is now a single straight vertical drop out of the bottom of the channel; the control-pilot interface sits to the right of that drop, so its line to the vehicle connector runs right and up with nothing in its way. FIG. 4's geometry prose no longer names shapes by reference numeral: the numerals are stripped before the geometry is drawn and reviewed, which is why the reviewer read sentences with holes in them ("the line from to leaves the lower vertex of"); shapes are now identified by position. content.text:
I fixed the one verified finding with the gate's preferred remedy (option one): the sensing connection is depicted in FIG. 2 as a branch off the already-depicted isolated local bus, so claim 1's "controller coupled to ... the connector current sensors" and the corresponding description sentence are now shown in the only view that breaks out a channel interior. No claim, description, numeral-table or FIG. 1/FIG. 3 change was needed, and none was made.

Two patches, both to `figures/FIG-2.md`:

1. Pinned the control-pilot interface block horizontally to the right of the connector current sensor circle, so the new vertical branch has an unambiguous, collision-free place to land on the bus.
2. Added the sensing branch itself, with explicit endpoint, ordering and no-crossing constraints matching the style of the existing branches.

Numeral 124 still ends on the *upper* part of the circle outline, so its leader cannot collide with the new branch, which terminates on the lower part.

One note on the record, per the drafting brief: no prior-art search was run for this application, and the art in `prior_art/` may be incomplete — the claim set has not been tested against a full search.

This follows the gate's stated primary remedy: the connection is carried on the already-depicted isolated local bus 108, consistent with the open-ended description sentence "carries communications between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, including ...", so FIG. 1, FIG. 3, the drawing descriptions, the detailed description, the claims and the 25-entry numeral table are unchanged byte for byte. Numeral 124 still terminates on the upper part of the circle outline and cannot collide with the new branch. No rendered artifact was touched; the drawing pipeline re-renders and re-inspects FIG. 2 from the amended brief. Separately, as the drafting brief requires: no prior-art search was run for this application, so the art supplied may be incomplete and the claims have not been tested against a full search.

structured_output.summary: Resolved the single verified finding (FIG. 2 omitted the controller-to-connector-current-sensor coupling recited in claim 1 and asserted in the detailed description) by amending only the FIG. 2 figure brief. A further vertical branch now rises from the isolated local bus line to the lower part of the connector current sensor circle outline, depicting the sensing connection by which the edge controller reads that sensor, and the control-pilot interface block is pinned horizontally to the right of the circle so the new branch lands on the bus between the contactor branch and that block without crossing any line work. This follows the gate's stated primary remedy: the connection is carried on the already-depicted isolated local bus 108, consistent with the open-ended description sentence "carries communications between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, including ...", so FIG. 1, FIG. 3, the drawing descriptions, the detailed description, the claims and the 25-entry numeral table are unchanged byte for byte. Numeral 124 still terminates on the upper part of the circle outline and cannot collide with the new branch. No rendered artifact was touched; the drawing pipeline re-renders and re-inspects FIG. 2 from the amended brief. Separately, as the drafting brief requires: no prior-art search was run for this application, so the art supplied may be incomplete and the claims have not been tested against a full search.
